info.title: YOB Storefront & Auth API — frontend contract
info.description:
Frappe RPC API. Every response is wrapped by Frappe in an outer `message` object; inside is the YOB envelope (`data` plus optional `notice`/`meta` on success, `errors[]` on failure). There is no `success` boolean: branch on HTTP status, then `errors[0].code`.

Authenticated storefront endpoints need the HttpOnly `sid` cookie and, for non-GET, `X-Frappe-CSRF-Token`.

The three payment endpoints are PUBLIC. `/payment/<token>` requires NO storefront session: `get_checkout_data` and `process_payment` are authorized by the checkout token, and `verify_payment` by Razorpay's HMAC signature. Do not place them behind a session guard.

See FRONTEND-CONTRACT.md for prose that this document cannot fully express.

OrderListRow.description: One row of `order.get_orders`. Exactly these six fields.

currency.description: the order's OWN stored currency -- never infer from environment configuration

discount_amount.description: (price_list_rate - rate) * qty, computed by the API

OrderPaymentLog.description: Razorpay Payment Log row, newest first. Empty for an unpaid or Pay Later order.

payment_method.description: the PROVIDER's method string ("netbanking", "card", ...). NOT the YOB Payment Method name sent to process_payment.

contact_email.description: from the Sales Order's stored field, NOT the Contact master. Frequently null on storefront orders.

billing_address_name.description: IDENTIFIER ONLY -- the linked Address master, which points at CURRENT data and may have been edited or deleted. Never render as the order's address.

billing_address_display.description: HISTORICAL. Plain text with real newlines -- never HTML, do not use [innerHTML]. Taken from the order's immutable order-time snapshot, so editing the Address master does not change a past order. `string | null` in every branch, never an object.

taxes.description: RAW ERPNext `Sales Taxes and Charges` child rows, passed through unprojected. Columns are ERPNext's and are NOT pinned by this contract; no real order observed so far has a tax row. Display only.

value._comment: HTTP 409. A Cart, a historical Sales Order, or the Customer default still references this address. It still EXISTS -- keep it in the list. Nothing is detached automatically, so this is not retryable. The referring document is deliberately not named.

errors.detail: This address is currently in use and can't be deleted.

post.description:
**AUTHENTICATED STOREFRONT**

Deletion is CONDITIONAL. Frappe refuses to delete a record another document still references.

- 200 -> deleted (`data` is `{}`)
- 404 `address_not_found` -> unknown, or not this customer's. Terminal.
- 409 `address_in_use` -> still referenced by a Cart, a historical Sales Order, or the Customer's default address. The record STILL EXISTS -- keep it in the list.

Nothing is detached automatically, so a 409 is NOT retryable: the user must change the selection first. The response carries only the code and a plain sentence; the referring document is deliberately not named.

DO NOT auto-retry a delete whose response was lost: the retry answers 404 and turns a success into an apparent error. Re-read the list instead.

value._comment: HTTP 409, the Contact mirror of delete-address-in-use-409. Previously this escaped as a raw Frappe LinkExistsError at HTTP 417 with Desk HTML in _server_messages.

errors.detail: This contact is currently in use and can't be deleted.

validation_failed.summary: 422 -- a required field was cleared, or a value rejected

value._comment: Sent { name, city: "" } -- an explicit clear of a REQUIRED field. The record is untouched. `field` names what to fix; previously this was a generic 500 with no field.

post.description:
**AUTHENTICATED STOREFRONT**

**PARTIAL UPDATE.** Send `name` plus only the fields you are editing.

Semantics are keyed on request PRESENCE, not truthiness:
- omitted -> UNCHANGED (the stored value is preserved)
- supplied value -> validated and applied
- explicit empty string on an optional field -> CLEARED
- invalid value -> `validation_failed` (422), record untouched

DO NOT resend untouched optional fields to preserve them. That was a workaround for a real bug (this endpoint used to assign every field unconditionally and blanked whatever was omitted) and it is now HARMFUL: an explicit empty value is a deliberate clear.

Idempotent -- the same payload applied twice converges. `name` identifies the record and is not editable; changing the title renames nothing, so links from historical documents stay stable.

example._comment: email/phone are read back from the SAVED record. They previously echoed the request, so an omitted email reported null while the contact still had one.

post.description:
**AUTHENTICATED STOREFRONT**

**qty is a DELTA added to any existing line for this item_code -- it does NOT replace it. Line qty 2 + add qty 5 = 7, on ONE row. A quantity stepper must send the difference. NOT idempotent: a retry or double-submit adds twice. There is no absolute set-quantity endpoint.**

qty.description: qty is a DELTA added to any existing line for this item_code -- it does NOT replace it. Line qty 2 + add qty 5 = 7, on ONE row. A quantity stepper must send the difference. NOT idempotent: a retry or double-submit adds twice. There is no absolute set-quantity endpoint. Fractional values accepted.

get.description:
**AUTHENTICATED STOREFRONT**

`order_id` is REQUIRED. Omitting it answers 422 `validation_failed` with `field: "order_id"` -- it is not treated as "list all".

Scoped to the authenticated Customer server-side. Another customer's order and a non-existent order both answer 404 `order_not_found`, identically, so the response cannot be used to probe for other customers' orders.

**Addresses are historical snapshots.** `billing_address_display` and `shipping_address_display` are `string | null` PLAIN TEXT (real newlines, never HTML) taken from the order's immutable order-time snapshot -- editing the Address master does not change a past order. `billing_address_name` / `shipping_address_name` are identifiers only and point at the CURRENT master. The former `billing_address` / `shipping_address` OBJECTS were removed: they read the master live and made order history mutable.

`contact_*` likewise come from the order's stored fields, not the Contact master, and are frequently null.

**AUTHENTICATED STOREFRONT**

**Takes no parameters.** No filter, search, date range, page or limit exists; the whole list is returned every time.

**Ordered by `creation` DESCENDING -- newest order first.** The server sorts; render the array as received and do not re-sort client-side. The sort key is the creation timestamp, NOT `transaction_date`: same-day orders share a `transaction_date`, and `creation` is not in the response, so a client sort cannot reproduce the correct order.

Each row carries the Sales Order's OWN stored `currency`. Never infer order-list currency from environment configuration.
